paper.title: Equal Opportunity in Online Classification with Partial Feedback

settings.name_in_paper: Online classification with partial (apple tasting) feedback under per-round gamma-EFP fairness
unmapped: Apple-tasting feedback: true label observed only when the learner predicts +1
0-1 classification loss; competes with best gamma-EFP (equalized false positive rate) convex combination of classifiers from a finite hypothesis class H (|H| = N_exp)
Learner must satisfy (gamma+beta)-EFP fairness w.r.t. the true distribution at every round with probability 1-delta
Access to a cost-sensitive classification oracle over H (oracle efficiency)
settings.definition_quote: In each round t, Learner chooses a convex combination \pi_t \in \Delta(\H). Environment draws (x_t,y_t) \sim D independently; learner observes x_t. Learner labels the point \hat{y}_t = h_t(x_t), where h_t \sim \pi_t. If \hat{y}_t = +1, Learner observes y_t.

settings.name_in_paper: Online classification with partial feedback under per-round fairness (lower bound)
unmapped: Learner must satisfy T^{-alpha}-EFP(delta) at every round; regret measured against 0-EFP fair policies
settings.definition_quote: There exists a hypothesis class H containing {\pm 1} such that any algorithm satisfying a T^{-\alpha}-EFP(\delta) fairness constraint has expected regret with respect to the set of 0-EFP fair policies of \Omega(T^{2\alpha}).

algorithms.name: Oracle-efficient fair algorithm (pure +1 exploration, FairCSC oracle, modified ILOVETOCONBANDITS)
Modified ILOVETOCONBANDITS with approximate CSC oracle

symbols.gamma: fairness level of the comparator class

source.label: upper
source.quote: For any $\H$ and data distribution satisfying the two mild assumptions above, there exists an oracle-efficient algorithm that takes parameters $\delta \in [0,\frac{1}{\sqrt{T}}]$ and $\gamma \geq 0$ as input and satisfies $(\gamma + \beta)$-EFP($\delta$) fairness and has an expected regret at most $\tilde O(\sqrt{T} \ln(|\H|/\delta) )$ with respect to the class of $\gamma$-EFP fair policies, where $\beta =  O(\sqrt{\ln(|\H|/\delta)}/T^{1/4})$.

results.notes: Regret defined as pseudo-regret w.r.t. the true distribution. Oracle-efficient = polynomial time given CSC oracle.

conditions: same two mild assumptions as Theorem 3.1

source.quote: More generally, we can extend Theorem~\ref{upper} to give an algorithm that satisfies $(\gamma + \beta)$-EFP($\delta$) for any $\beta > 0$, and achieves an expected regret at most $\tilde O\left(\frac{\ln(\frac{|\H|}{\delta})}{\beta^2} + \sqrt{T} \ln(|\H|/\delta) \right)$ with respect to the class of $\gamma$-EFP fair policies.

results.notes: Stated as a remark without proof.

symbols.alpha_f: tradeoff exponent; fairness gap gamma'-gamma = O(T^{-alpha_f})

tuning: exploration length modified according to alpha_f

source.quote: it is straightforward, by modifying the length of the exploration round, to obtain a more general tradeoff---a regret bound of $O(T^{2\alpha})$ with respect to the set of $\gamma$-EFP fair policies, while satisfying $(\gamma + O(T^{-\alpha}))$-EFP($\delta$) fairness, for any $\alpha \in [1/4,1/2]$.

results.notes: Remark without proof; log factors suppressed.

conditions: regret measured against best policy in Pi (support-2 empirically fair mixtures)
given access to an approximate-CSC oracle

source.label: thm:bandit-regret
source.quote: The bandit algorithm, given access to an approximate-CSC oracle, runs in time polynomial in $T$ and achieves expected regret at most $O\left(\ln(|\H|T/\delta) ~ \sqrt{T}\right)$.

results.notes: Comparator is the policy class Pi, not the gamma-EFP class; intermediate result for Theorem 3.1.

conditions: hard hypothesis class H = {-1,+1,h_1,h_2} with two indistinguishable distributions

source.label: thm:main-negative1
source.quote: Fix any $\alpha \in (0,0.5)$ and let $T \geq \sqrt[\alpha]{16}$. Fix any $\delta \leq 0.24$. There exists a hypothesis class $\H$ containing $\{\pm \mathbf{1}\}$ such that any algorithm satisfying a $T^{-\alpha}$-EFP($\delta$) fairness constraint has expected  regret with respect to the set of 0-EFP fair policies of $\Omega\left(T^{2\alpha}\right)$.

results.notes: Algorithm class: all algorithms satisfying the per-round fairness constraint. Proof via KL/Pinsker between two distributions.
